spec.description: Live NVIDIA GPU Operator and DCGM exporter observability. Covers all 23 active DCGM metric families and GPU Operator health metrics; every panel has a Grafana hover-info description.

spec.title: GPU Operator node-upgrade states
spec.description: Number of GPU nodes in each Operator-managed driver-upgrade state: available, pending, in progress, done, or failed. It is an upgrade workflow view, not a health check for GPU workloads.

spec.title: Physical GPUs in scope
spec.description: Number of distinct physical GPU UUIDs selected. It is derived from the GPU-utilization series and deduplicated by node, UUID, and GPU index to guard against duplicate scrape series.

spec.title: Average GPU utilization
spec.description: Device-wide percentage of time the GPU was busy during the sample (0–100%). It is utilization, not a Kubernetes GPU request and not a per-container share.

spec.title: Average GPU core temperature
spec.description: Current GPU core temperature in degrees Celsius. This is a device sensor reading; use it with power and clocks rather than assuming a universal thermal limit.

spec.title: Framebuffer pressure
spec.description: Percentage of usable device framebuffer currently used: used divided by used plus free. Reserved framebuffer is intentionally excluded because it is driver-reserved, not workload-allocatable VRAM.

spec.expr: 100 * sum(max by (hostname, UUID, gpu, modelName) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED{job="dcgm-exporter"})) / (sum(max by (hostname, UUID, gpu, modelName) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED{job="dcgm-exporter"})) + sum(max by (hostname, UUID, gpu, modelName) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE{job="dcgm-exporter"})))

spec.title: Total GPU power draw
spec.description: Sum of instantaneous device-board power draw in watts across the selected physical GPUs. It is a current sample, not energy consumed over the time range.

spec.title: Energy in selected range
spec.description: Energy consumed in the dashboard's selected time range, derived from the cumulative DCGM energy counter. Source units are millijoules; the result is watt-hours. The counter resets after a GPU or driver restart.

spec.title: GPU identity and workload mapping
spec.description: GPU identity, driver version, and Kubernetes workload labels reported by DCGM. Prometheus renames workload labels to exported_namespace, exported_pod, and exported_container to avoid collisions with the exporter target labels.

spec.expr: max by (hostname, UUID, gpu, modelName, pci_bus_id, device, namespace, pod, container) (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL{job="dcgm-exporter"})

spec.title: GPU utilization
spec.description: Device-wide percentage of time the GPU was busy during each sample (0–100%). It does not measure a pod's GPU request, a per-container share, FLOPS, or scheduler allocation.

spec.title: Compute and DRAM profiler activity
spec.description: DCGM profiler ratios rendered as percent: graphics/compute engine active time, tensor-pipe active cycles, and DRAM-interface active cycles. Tensor activity is not FLOPS; DRAM activity is not VRAM allocation. Availability depends on profiling support.

spec.title: Memory-copy, encode, and decode engines
spec.description: Percentage of time the GPU memory-copy, video encoder, and video decoder engines were busy (0–100%). High copy activity can indicate data-transfer pressure; zero encode/decode is normal for many inference and training workloads.

spec.title: SM and memory clocks
spec.description: Current streaming-multiprocessor and memory clock frequencies. DCGM exports MHz; queries convert to Hz so Grafana can render GHz. Idle behavior, power policy, and thermal limits can all reduce clocks.

spec.title: Framebuffer capacity split
spec.description: On-device framebuffer memory split into used, free, and driver-reserved capacity across the selected physical-GPU scope. DCGM exports MiB; the query converts to bytes for human-readable Grafana scaling. This is physical device VRAM, not pod RAM.

spec.title: GPU and memory temperature
spec.description: Current GPU core and memory-sensor temperature in degrees Celsius. A memory-temperature value of 0 can mean the sensor is unsupported or unavailable; it does not mean the memory is cold. Treat core temperature as the primary thermal signal.

spec.title: Board power and energy-derived power
spec.description: Instantaneous board power draw in watts alongside a moving average derived from the cumulative energy counter. The two should broadly agree; the energy-derived series uses rate(counter)/1000 because DCGM energy is millijoules.

spec.title: Cumulative GPU energy since boot
spec.description: Cumulative energy consumption since boot or the current driver/GPU lifetime. DCGM exports millijoules; this panel converts to watt-hours. A reset is expected after a device or driver restart, so compare deltas rather than assuming a permanent lifetime total.

spec.title: Operator reconciliation
spec.description: GPU Operator ClusterPolicy convergence result. 1 means reconciled; 0 means operands are not ready; -1 means the policy is unavailable; -2 means an operator error. This is control-plane health, not a statement that the GPU is busy.

spec.title: PCIe transmit and receive throughput
spec.description: Instantaneous PCIe throughput from the GPU perspective, in bytes per second and including headers plus payload. Transmit is generally device-to-host and receive host-to-device. These DCGM fields are already rates; PromQL rate() would be wrong.

spec.title: PCIe replay events in selected range
spec.description: Total increase in the cumulative PCIe retry/replay counter over the selected dashboard range and physical-GPU scope. Sustained growth can indicate PCIe link quality or signal-integrity issues. Counter lifecycle behavior can vary with GPU or driver resets.

spec.title: Correctable and uncorrectable row remaps
spec.description: Cumulative framebuffer row remaps caused by correctable and uncorrectable memory errors. Rising counts consume hardware spare rows and warrant investigation; uncorrectable growth is more serious. Treat these as persistent hardware-health state, not a transient workload metric.

spec.title: Row-remap failure flag
spec.description: Whether the GPU could not remap a failed framebuffer row. 1 means a remap failure was reported; 0 means no remap failure. Treat any nonzero value as hardware risk.

spec.title: vGPU license status
spec.description: Vendor vGPU-license status code. 0 means not licensed and 1 means licensed. Interpret this only for a vGPU deployment; a bare-metal or pass-through A10 can legitimately report 0 and it is not a GPU-health failure.

spec.title: GPU Compute Efficiency Ratio
spec.description: Ratio of core computing utilization compared to overall board wattage. Higher numbers indicate better batch size optimization and less CPU/Disk bottlenecking.

spec.title: Time since last successful reconciliation
spec.description: Age of the most recent successful GPU Operator reconciliation. A rapidly growing value means the controller is no longer recording successful convergence.

spec.title: GPU nodes known to the operator
spec.description: Count of GPU nodes discovered by the GPU Operator. It validates the operator's view of GPU-capable Kubernetes nodes, not a GPU allocation count.

spec.title: NFD labels present
spec.description: Whether GPU Operator reconciliation sees the Node Feature Discovery labels it needs. 1 means labels are present; 0 means discovery/labeling is incomplete.

spec.title: Driver auto-upgrade
spec.description: GPU Operator driver auto-upgrade switch. It governs whether the operator automatically updates the NVIDIA driver operand; it is not an indication of a driver update being available.

spec.title: DCGM scrape health
spec.description: Prometheus reachability of the GPU Operator DCGM exporter. A value of 1 means telemetry is being collected; 0 means a discovered target is failing. If no target is discovered, Grafana shows No data rather than 0. The query deliberately pins job=nvidia-dcgm-exporter so any other exporter cannot be double-counted.

spec.title: GPU Operator reconciliation activity
spec.description: Per-second GPU Operator reconciliation attempts and failures, derived from cumulative counters. A rising failed line is material even if the current reconciliation-status gauge is 1.

spec.title: NVIDIA GPU Operator & DCGM Observability
